race_context: The district: the 'Jackson Seymour City Community School Board' seats belong to Seymour Community Schools (Seymour Community School Corporation), based in Seymour in Jackson County {nces_scsc}{scsc_board}. Federal data list 5,432 students in eight schools in 2024-25 {nces_scsc}. Brandon Harpe is superintendent {scsc_board}; in September 2025 the board recognized him as the Indiana Association of Public School Superintendents' District 8 Superintendent of the Year {scsc_min_20250909}.

The board: the Board of School Trustees has seven members {scsc_board}{scsc_min_20250812}. State election results list its seats by area: a Seymour City Seat 1, two Seymour City at-large seats ('Seats 1 & 2, At Large'), and seats for Hamilton, Jackson, Redding and Washington townships {enr_2020}{enr_2022}{enr_2024}. In December 2022 the superintendent described one departing member as 'the Seymour City At-Large representative' and another as 'the Jackson Township representative' {scsc_min_20221213}. This guide did not find the district's own description of who may vote in each race.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: this race fills TWO seats, not one. The state list shows 'vote for 1', but the same office ('Jackson Seymour City Community School Board, Seats 1 & 2, At Large') was a two-seat race in 2022, when Joe Tormoehlen (3,820 votes) and Holly Coates (3,292) won both seats over incumbent Nancy Franke (2,880) {in_list}{enr_2022}. With two candidates for two seats, the race is uncontested. Voters should check their sample ballot for how many candidates to choose.

Who holds the seats now: both candidates are incumbents. Tormoehlen took the oath of office for a new term in January 2023, and Coates attended her first board meeting the same month {scsc_min_20230110}. In January 2026 the board re-elected Tormoehlen vice president and Coates secretary, each by a 7-0 vote; Ken Browning is president {scsc_min_20260113}{scsc_board}. Both filed for re-election on May 19, 2026 {incitizen_list}.

Other Seymour seats on the 2026 ballot appear as separate races on the state list: Redding Township (John Kelley, the current member) and Washington Township (Jeff Hubbard) {in_list}{incitizen_list}. Max Klosterman, who won the Washington Township seat in 2022, is not on the 2026 list {enr_2022}{in_list}.
Party labels: Holly Coates is listed as a Republican and Joe Tormoehlen as nonpartisan on the state list {in_list}. Both ran without party labels in 2022 {enr_2022}.

Board vacancy: longtime member Art Juergens, who held the Seymour City Seat 1 and was re-elected in 2024, died in early February 2026 {enr_2024}{scsc_min_20260210}. Superintendent Harpe said Juergens was first elected in 2008, served ten years as board president and earlier taught history and social studies at Seymour High School from 1979 to 2008 {scsc_min_20260210}. On February 19, 2026 the board voted 6-0 to appoint Dr. Charles Calhoun, the only applicant, as interim Seymour City board member {scsc_min_20260219}. That seat is not on the 2026 ballot {in_list}.

Construction and bonds: the board regularly approves payments for projects funded by 2024 and 2025 bonds {scsc_min_20250812}{scsc_min_20260210}. In February 2026 it voted 5-0 to award roof replacements at Jackson Elementary ($405,500) and at Seymour High School and Seymour Intermediate ($338,329), new Seymour High School tennis courts ($896,400) and a Seymour Middle School administration renovation ($2,171,529) {scsc_min_20260210}. In September 2025 the district's assistant superintendent recommended a $4,730,000 low bid from Harrell-Fish, Inc. for Seymour Middle School HVAC work {scsc_min_20250909}.

Proposed new bond issue: in June 2026 the district gave notice of hearings on July 8 and July 22, 2026 on a long-term capital improvement project covering roofs, HVAC, life-safety and security improvements, paving, pool and site work, and buses, vehicles, equipment and technology; at the second hearing the board was to consider a preliminary determination to enter into leases and/or issue bonds to pay for it {scsc_notice_20260624}. At the July 8 hearing, the estimated costs and potential tax rate impact were presented and no members of the public spoke; the minutes do not give the dollar amounts {scsc_min_20260708}. Minutes of the July 22 hearing were not posted when this guide was prepared.

Budget and taxes: the board held its 2026 budget hearing on September 23, 2025 (no public comments) and adopted the 2026 budget on October 14, 2025 {scsc_min_20250923}{scsc_min_20251014}. For 2027, it scheduled a budget hearing for September 22, 2026 and adoption for October 6, 2026 {scsc_min_20260811}. At an August 19, 2026 work session it reviewed the education, debt service and operations funds and a proposed five-year bus replacement plan {scsc_min_20260819}. This guide found no public statement from the board on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Seymour's budget. Seymour is not listed among districts with referendums on the November 2026 ballot {dlgf_ref}.

Staffing and other actions: in November 2025 the board approved, 6-0, the 2025-26 master teacher contract with the Seymour Education Association and a $250,000 transfer from the education fund to the self-insurance fund; it also approved 2026 health insurance with a rate increase {scsc_min_20251111}. In December 2025 it approved a three-year school calendar for 2026-2029, 7-0 {scsc_min_20251209}. In August 2026 it approved a state policy update on artificial intelligence, 6-0 {scsc_min_20260811}. During public comment in November and December 2025, a community member raised concerns about how the district carries out its staff mental-health procedures and handles medical-leave paperwork {scsc_min_20251111}{scsc_min_20251209}.
Votes recorded in the 2025-26 minutes reviewed for this guide were unanimous, with occasional abstentions by individual members on specific items {scsc_min_20250812}{scsc_min_20250909}.

Forums and questionnaires: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, newspaper questionnaire or VOTE411 entry for this race. Local newspaper coverage from the Seymour Tribune could not be read for this guide.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, first elected in 2022 and serving as board secretary; running unopposed with Joe Tormoehlen for the two at-large seats {enr_2022}{scsc_min_20260113}.
background: Won one of the two Seymour City at-large seats in 2022, unseating incumbent Nancy Franke, and joined the board in January 2023 {enr_2022}{scsc_min_20230110}.
Elected board secretary by 7-0 votes in January 2026 {scsc_min_20260113}. Serves on the Board of Finance and as the board's public and community relations appointee {scsc_min_20260113}.
path_to_ballot: Listed as a Republican on the state list {in_list}.
on_incumbent: In board comments she has thanked staff for preparing buildings for the school year and praised the district's back-to-school communications and social media {scsc_min_20250812}{scsc_min_20250909}{scsc_min_20260811}. In February 2026 she said Art Juergens' loyalty to the district 'will be greatly missed' {scsc_min_20260210}.

Voted with the majority on the construction awards, budget, calendar and policy items recorded in the 2025-26 minutes reviewed for this guide {scsc_min_20260210}{scsc_min_20251209}{scsc_min_20260811}.
